Hood III, William W. 2026 Evaluation
 Colorado Supreme CourtHonorable William W. Hood IIIRetention Year: 2026Recommendation: Meets Performance Standards
 Reports: 2026 Retention Survey Report (PDF)2023 Interim Survey Report (PDF)
 The State Commission on Judicial Performance finds that Justice William W. Hood III, by vote of 9-0 with one commissioner absent, and one commission vacancy, MEETS PERFORMANCE STANDARDS. The Colorado statutory judicial performance standards are integrity, legal knowledge, communication skills, judicial temperament, administrative performance, and service to the legal profession and the public.Justice Hood has served on the Colorado Supreme Court since January 2014.  The Commission finds that Justice Hood is courteous to attorneys and treats parties equally without regard to race, sex, or economic status.  He demonstrates an admirable work ethic and issues decisions in a timely manner.  During oral arguments, he is respectful of the attorneys and their allotted time, and he asks insightful questions.  His opinions are well organized, and he has a clear writing style that makes the reader’s job easier.  The Commission believes that Justice Hood is a valuable member of the Colorado Supreme Court.To conduct our evaluation, the Commission interviewed Justice Hood, reviewed his self-evaluation, observed oral arguments, read a selection of his legal opinions, and considered survey responses from attorneys and judges.  A total of 7 attorneys and 24 judges responded to the survey; overall, respondents affirmed that Justice Hood meets performance standards.Before joining the Colorado Supreme Court, Justice Hood spent seven years as a judge on the Denver District Court. Before becoming a judge, Justice Hood was a litigation partner at a Denver law firm and served as a prosecutor for ten years in Colorado’s 18th Judicial District.  Justice Hood graduated from the University of Virginia School of Law and Syracuse University.  In 2014, the Colorado Chapter of the American Academy of Matrimonial Lawyers gave him its Distinguished Jurist Award. In 2011, he received the Denver Bar Association’s (DBA’s) Judicial Excellence Award. He is a 2007 graduate of the Colorado Bar Association’s leadership training program (COBALT). He has also taught several courses related to advocacy as an adjunct faculty member at the University of Denver Sturm College of Law.

Freyre, Rebecca Rankin 2026 Evaluation
 Colorado Court of AppealsHonorable Rebecca Rankin FreyreRetention Year: 2026Recommendation: Meets Performance Standards
 Reports: 2026 Retention Survey Report (PDF)2023 Interim Survey Report (PDF)
 The State Commission on Judicial Performance finds that Judge Rebecca Rankin Freyre, by vote of 9-0 with one commissioner absent, and one commission vacancy, MEETS PERFORMANCE STANDARDS. Colorado’s statutory judicial performance standards are integrity, legal knowledge, communication skills, judicial temperament, and service to the legal profession and the public.Judge Freyre was appointed to the Colorado Court of Appeals in 2015 and has served with distinction for 11 years. She successfully stood for retention in 2018 and has now served a full eight-year term. The Commission finds her written opinions to be thoughtful, well-reasoned, and drafted with clarity that makes the information accessible to litigants, practitioners, and the public. We find her judicial demeanor at oral arguments to be respectful, engaging, and present. Judge Freyre served as the Deputy Chief Judge from January 2022 to January 2026. She currently chairs the PERA Board and sustains a broad range of civic and volunteer commitments to serve the legal profession and the public, including providing mentorship to law students and emerging judges. In summary, the Commission finds Judge Freyre to be an exemplary jurist and a valuable member of the Court of Appeals.To conduct its evaluation, the Commission interviewed Judge Freyre, reviewed her self-evaluation, observed oral arguments, examined a selection of her legal opinions, and considered survey responses from attorneys and judges. Every survey respondent agreed that Judge Freyre meets applicable judicial performance standards. She received positive comments from respondents with respect to her strong writing skills, astute oral argument questions, strong legal analysis for reaching fair outcomes in gray areas, and her receptiveness and incorporation of feedback from her fellow judges.Judge Freyre earned her undergraduate degree in Economics at Smith College and her law degree from the University of Denver College of Law. She began her career in law as a law clerk at a private criminal defense firm in Denver, Colorado before dedicating 25 years as a Deputy State Public Defender, working in the Appellate Division in Denver and the Trial Office in Arapahoe County before appointment to the bench in 2015.

Harris, Elizabeth L. 2026 Evaluation
 Colorado Court of AppealsHonorable Elizabeth L. HarrisRetention Year: 2026Recommendation: Meets Performance Standards
 Reports: 2026 Retention Survey Report (PDF)2023 Interim Survey Report (PDF)
 The State Commission on Judicial Performance finds that Judge Elizabeth L. Harris, by vote of 9-0 with one commissioner absent, and one commission vacancy, MEETS PERFORMANCE STANDARDS. Colorado’s statutory judicial performance standards are integrity, legal knowledge, communication skills, judicial temperament, and service to the legal profession and the public.The Commission finds that her opinions are clear, well-written, and reasonably timely. At oral arguments, she is well-prepared, succinct in her questions, respectful, and seeks to draw out the issues most important to the Court’s decision-making process. Judge Harris received positive comments from lawyers about her preparation, intelligence, familiarity with the record on appeal, and knowledge of the law.  Lawyers noted the length of time required for Judge Harris to issue an opinion as a weakness.  Judge Harris received positive comments from fellow judges for her writing ability, her thoughtfulness and her engagement in committee work for Colorado Courts. Judges also noted Judge Harris’ timeliness in issuing decisions as a weakness. The Commission commends Judge Harris for her commitment to community service and the Court of Appeals/Supreme Court summer internship program.  Such efforts beyond the daily work of the Court of Appeals demonstrate dedication to serving the legal profession and the public. In sum, the Commission finds Judge Harris to be a valuable member of the Court of Appeals.To conduct our evaluation, the Commission interviewed Judge Harris, reviewed her self-evaluation, observed oral arguments, read a selection of her legal opinions, and considered survey responses from attorneys and judges. The Commission received survey responses from only 5 attorneys and 22 judges.  Nevertheless, the Commission is confident in this opinion because 93% of responding judges and attorneys agreed, and all remaining sources of information available supported a finding that Judge Harris “Meets Performance Standards.”Judge Harris is a graduate of Georgetown University and New York University School ofLaw. She began her legal career as a law clerk for the Honorable John Porfilio of the United States Court of Appeals for the Tenth Circuit. After her clerkship, she spent five years at the Federal Public Defender’s Office in Colorado and then joined the law firm of Jacobs Chase, which was later acquired by Husch Blackwell. In 2013, she opened her own law firm where she focused on appellate litigation. She was appointed to the Colorado Court of Appeals in 2015.

 Reports: 2026 Retention Survey Report (PDF)2025 Interim Survey Report (PDF)
 The State Commission on Judicial Performance finds that Judge Katharine E. Lum, by vote of 9-0 with one commissioner absent, and one commission vacancy, MEETS PERFORMANCE STANDARDS. Colorado’s statutory judicial performance standards are integrity, legal knowledge, communication skills, judicial temperament, and service to the legal profession and the public.Judge Lum was appointed to the Colorado Court of Appeals in 2022 and has served for four years. This is her first time standing for retention. The Commission finds she embodies the qualities of an outstanding appellate judge and is a valuable asset to the Colorado Court of Appeals. Her opinions are fair and thoughtful, and she delivers well-reasoned decisions based on the law and facts. She is an exceptional judicial writer who conveys her opinions in a clear and accessible style understood by litigants, practitioners, and members of the public alike. She arrives well-prepared to oral arguments, and is engaged, present, and respectful in the Courtroom. She also serves as the Liaison to the 15th Judicial District. Beyond her duties as a judge, she participates in community service activities that advance the court’s mission.The Commission conducted its evaluation of Judge Lum by considering her self-evaluation, observing her oral arguments, examining a selection of her legal opinions (including dissents), conducting an in-person interview with her, and reviewing survey responses submitted by attorneys and judges. Every survey respondent agreed that Judge Lum meets performance standards. She received positive feedback in regard to her strong listening, polite and respectful nature, and thorough preparation.Judge Lum earned her JD from the University of California Berkeley School of Law. Prior to joining the bench, she was Of Counsel with Cooper Ramp Cage Bucar Lewis (and predecessor firms) where she specialized in domestic relations law at the trial and appellate levels; and she clerked for the Honorable Gregory J. Hobbs Jr. of the Colorado Supreme Court. She serves on the Supreme Court Standing Committee on Family Issues; as the Court of Appeals liaison and coordinator for a long-standing externship program with Colorado law schools; and as a board member of the Minoru Yasui Inn of Court.

Moultrie, Pax 2026 Evaluation
 Colorado Court of AppealsHonorable Pax MoultrieRetention Year: 2026Recommendation: Meets Performance Standards
 Reports: 2026 Retention Survey Report (PDF)2025 Interim Survey Report (PDF)
 The State Commission on Judicial Performance unanimously finds by a vote of 9-0, with one commission absence and one commission vacancy, that Judge Pax Moultrie MEETS PERFORMANCE STANDARDS. Colorado’s statutory judicial performance standards are integrity, legal knowledge, communication skills, judicial temperament, and service to the legal profession and the public.Judge Moultrie was appointed to the Colorado Court of Appeals in January 2024, and this is her first time standing for retention as a Court of Appeals Judge. The Commission finds that her opinions are thoughtful, accessible, and well written. At oral argument, she has an excellent judicial demeanor, engages with the attorneys, and is respectful of all parties. The Commission commends Judge Moultrie for her service to the judicial branch’s well-being efforts to support judicial officers and employees as well as her efforts to educate the community about the courts. In sum, the Commission finds Judge Moultrie is a valuable addition to the Court of Appeals.To conduct its evaluation, the Commission interviewed Judge Moultrie, reviewed her self-evaluation, observed oral arguments, read a selection of her legal opinions, and considered survey responses from attorneys and judges. Every surveyed respondent agreed that Judge Moultrie meets Colorado’s Judicial Performance Standards. She received positive comments from lawyers with respect to her courteous demeanor during oral arguments and her ability to write in plain language so that both lawyers and laypersons can understand her opinions. Judge Moultrie received positive comments from fellow judges, especially with respect to the valuable perspective she brings as a former juvenile court judge.Judge Moultrie earned her bachelor’s degree from Washington University in St. Louis and her law degree from the University of Denver Sturm College of Law. She began her legal career as a law clerk in the 1st Judicial District, which was followed by a clerkship with the Colorado Supreme Court. She then represented county departments of human services in dependency and neglect matters and juvenile delinquency matters. Before joining the Court of Appeals, she served as a district court judge for Denver Juvenile Court, where she presided over a docket consisting of dependency and neglect cases, juvenile delinquency cases, and adoptions. She also previously served as a magistrate in the 1st Judicial District. She is a member of several specialty bar associations, including the Sam Cary Bar Association and the Colorado Women’s Bar Association. She is a Fellow of the Colorado Bar Foundation and is a founding member of the Irving P. Andrews Inn of Court. Judge Moultrie has served as an appointed board member of law-related and community non-profit organizations and is currently active in the Colorado Judicial Branch’s well-being efforts to support judicial officers and employees.

 Reports: 2026 Retention Survey Report (PDF)2025 Interim Survey Report (PDF)
 The State Commission on Judicial Performance finds that Judge Karl L. Schock, by vote of 9-0 with one commissioner absent, and one commission vacancy, MEETS PERFORMANCE STANDARDS. Colorado’s statutory judicial performance standards are integrity, legal knowledge, communication skills, judicial temperament, and service to the legal profession and the public.Judge Schock was appointed to the Colorado Court of Appeals in 2022 and has served for four years. The Commission finds that he has the qualities of an excellent Court of Appeals judge. His written opinions are clear and easy to understand. At oral argument, he is respectful, curious, and well-prepared on both the facts and the law. He also serves on committees that work on model criminal jury instructions and probation services, which helps improve the courts.To reach its decision, the Commission interviewed Judge Schock; reviewed his self-evaluation; watched several oral arguments; and read many of his opinions, concurrences, and dissents. It also reviewed survey responses from attorneys and judges. Every person surveyed agreed that Judge Schock meets Colorado’s judicial performance standards. Many praised his clear writing. Some noted that his separate concurrences and dissents show care in his work. Others said his questions at oral argument made them feel he took their legal issues seriously.Judge Schock earned his undergraduate degree from Northern Arizona University and his law degree from the University of Colorado in 2006. He then clerked for Judge Michael Murphy on the United States Court of Appeals for the Tenth Circuit. After clerking, he joined the law firm Brownstein Hyatt Farber Schreck until 2015 when he served as an Assistant U.S. Attorney in the Appellate Division before being appointed to the bench in 2022.

Sullivan, Grant 2026 Evaluation
 Colorado Court of AppealsHonorable Grant SullivanRetention Year: 2026Recommendation: Meets Performance Standards
 Reports: 2026 Retention Survey Report (PDF)2025 Interim Survey Report (PDF)
 The State Commission on Judicial Performance finds that Judge Grant Sullivan, by vote of 9-0 with one commissioner absent, and one commission vacancy, MEETS PERFORMANCE STANDARDS. The judicial performance standards include integrity, legal knowledge, communication skills, judicial temperament, administrative performance, and service to the legal profession and the public.Judge Sullivan began service on the Colorado Court of Appeals in January of 2024. The Commission found the judge’s written opinions to be consistently well-reasoned, fair, and thoughtfully articulated, demonstrating a strong command of the law and clear judicial reasoning. Although Judge Sullivan joined the Court of Appeals in January 2024, the Commission notes a strong and confident transition into the role of appellate judge. The judge has proactively established systems to manage workload efficiently and collaborates regularly with judicial colleagues, reflecting a dedication to continuous improvement and excellence in service.As part of this evaluation, the Commission conducted a thorough review of Judge Sullivan’s performance. This included an in-depth interview with the judge, a review of selected legal opinions, courtroom observations, analysis of the judicial performance survey report, and a review of the judge’s self-evaluation. Judge Sullivan was observed to be clear, open, and highly effective in communication, and consistently maintained courtroom decorum. While appropriately assertive in managing proceedings, the judge’s tone and demeanor remained balanced, reflecting impartiality and professionalism. These qualities contribute meaningfully to the public’s confidence in the judiciary. Judge Sullivan’s self-evaluation and interview reflected a deep commitment to timely, transparent, and respectful engagement with all parties, an approach that aligns with courtroom observations and stakeholder feedback. Judge Sullivan practiced law as a trial and appellate litigator with the Colorado Attorney General’s Office, specializing in constitutional law, voting rights, election law, tax, administrative law, and appeals. He previously practiced law with the Denver office of a national firm and served as a Supreme Court Fellow with the National Association of Attorneys General. He clerked on both the Colorado Court of Appeals and the Colorado Supreme Court. Judge Sullivan earned his Juris Doctorate from the University of Colorado Law School and his Bachelor of Business Administration degree from the University of Texas at Austin. In addition to his duties as a judge on the Court of Appeals, Judge Sullivan participates in the Court of Appeals’ “Courts in the Community” program and serves on numerous court committees (including the Judicial Department’s Reclassification Review Board, an Appellate Rules Subcommittee, and a planning committee for the annual Colorado Judicial Conference). He also volunteers as a guest coach and judge for the CU Mock Trial and Moot Court programs and volunteers with the Food Bank of the Rockies.

Contiguglia, Chantel E. 2026 Evaluation 
Contiguglia, Chantel E. 2026 Evaluation 
 First Judicial District - District Court JudgeHonorable Chantel E. ContigugliaRetention Year: 2026Recommendation: Meets Performance Standards
 Reports: 2026 Retention Survey Report (PDF)2025 Interim Survey Report (PDF)
 The First Judicial District Commission on Judicial Performance unanimously (10-0) finds Judge Chantel E. Contiguglia MEETS PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.Judge Contiguglia was appointed to the District Court in Jefferson County on January 1, 2024.  She presides over a mixed docket of criminal, civil and domestic relations matters. Judge Contiguglia has been described as prepared, fair, consistent, and respectful with good judicial demeanor and temperament.   She is thoughtful and sets clear deadlines and expectations.  Her case management was described as efficient; however it was noted her scheduling practices could be inflexible for trial and docket management, which has been perceived by some litigants to overlook practical needs of the parties.  During her interim evaluation Judge Contiguglia was given this feedback and since that time, there has been improvement.  Judge Contiguglia’s background is predominantly criminal defense work, which is reflected in her acumen with criminal law. Judge Contiguglia is committed to increasing her proficiency in civil and domestic relations law by seeking out colleagues with this expertise and attending continuing legal education in these areas. The Commission finds Judge Contiguglia meets performance standards and is pleased she has committed to increasing her proficiency in civil and domestic relations law.The commission conducted a personal interview with Judge Contiguglia, reviewed orders she authored, observed her in court, reviewed the judicial performance survey responses from attorneys, non-attorneys, jurors and court staff, and received feedback from the chief judge of the 1st Judicial District, the Office of the District Attorney, and the Office of the State Public Defender. There was a limited number of survey responses for this evaluation period.  Five appellate court judges responded to the survey and rated Judge Contiguglia high (4.0 out of 4.0).Judge Contiguglia grew up in Walden, Colorado, a small town in Jackson County.  She earned her Bachelor of Arts in Political Science from Mesa State College and her Juris Doctorate from the University of Denver in 2006.  Before her current appointment, she served as a County Court Judge in Arapahoe County for six years.  Prior to that Judge Contiguglia spent over ten years with the Colorado State Public Defender’s Office.  In addition to her public responsibilities, she remains committed to community service, frequently volunteering at local schools, mentoring young attorneys, and participating in programs that support access to justice.

Loewer, Ryan P. 2026 Evaluation 
 First Judicial District - District Court JudgeHonorable Ryan P. LoewerRetention Year: 2026Recommendation: Meets Performance Standards
 Reports: 2026 Retention Survey Report (PDF)2025 Interim Survey Report (PDF)
 The First Judicial District Commission on Judicial Performance unanimously agrees by a vote of 10-0, that Judge Ryan P. Loewer MEETS PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.Judge Loewer serves as a District Court Judge and presides over a mixed docket of domestic relations, civil, and criminal cases. Judge Loewer’s demeanor is described as formal, professional, dignified and fair.  Judge Loewer indicated to the Commission that he is working to balance the level of formality that he believes maintains decorum and expectations in his court with the need to make sure parties are not intimidated by the process. Judge Loewer makes a concerted effort to be organized and prepared for every court appearance and finds that assists him in efficiently managing his docket. Judge Loewer describes himself as hypervigilant in his efforts to avoid inappropriate bias and discrimination. As Judge Loewer gains additional experience, he recognizes he has room for improvement and is excited for the opportunities for growth that this provides. Judge Loewer’s orders are well written, thorough and reflect his attention to detail. Based on these findings the Commission unanimously agreed that Judge Loewer meets performance standards and is an asset to the District Court.The Commission conducted a personal interview with Judge Loewer, reviewed orders he authored, observed him in court, and reviewed judicial performance survey responses from attorneys, non-attorneys, and appellate judges who had interaction in Judge Loewer’s court. The Commission also received information from the District Attorney and the Office of the Public Defender regarding their offices’ opinions and experiences with Judge Loewer. Judge Loewer was appointed to the District Court in August 2023.Before presiding on the bench, he practiced criminal law for thirteen years as a deputy state public defender. He serves on the Colorado Judicial Education Committee, the Magistrate Wellness and Support Committee, and he presides as the district court judge for the 1st JD Fresh Start Program. He coaches other judges for the Colorado Judicial Peer-to-Peer Coaching Program. Judge Loewer is a graduate of and mentor for the Colorado Institute for Faculty Excellence—Judicial Education (COIFE-JE) and annually teaches at Advanced New Judge Orientation. He presents continuing legal education classes in the areas of overlapping issues of family and criminal law, indirect contempt practice, magistrate jurisdiction, rules of evidence, and attorney ethics. Judge Loewer attributes his interest in judging to his childhood hobbies of competitive livestock and dairy cattle judging.

Miloud, Meegan 2026 Evaluation 
 First Judicial District - District Court JudgeHonorable Meegan MiloudRetention Year: 2026Recommendation: Meets Performance Standards
 Reports: 2026 Retention Survey Report (PDF)2025 Interim Survey Report (PDF)
 The First Judicial District Commission on Judicial Performance agrees by a vote of 10-0 that the Honorable Meegan Miloud MEETS PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.After meeting with Judge Miloud, reviewing her work over the past three years, and assessing feedback from attorneys and non-attorneys, the Commission unanimously determined that she meets judicial performance standards. Among her many accomplishments, she successfully managed a backlogged docket and brought it current. She accomplished this while maintaining an efficient and effective workflow. Judge Miloud is noted for her calm demeanor and good communication both in verbal interactions with court participants as well as in her written orders.  She expresses understanding that parties that appear before her can be served best by having clarity and understanding of the process. To that end, Judge Miloud ensures that each party has ample time to ask questions and she provides proper instructions.  Further, she maintains decorum in her courtroom.  Judge Miloud is known for being well prepared. Her decisions are well-reasoned and she follows the law.  She has plans to continue to develop her skills in civil law by attending conferences and courses as well as accessing the mentorship available in the district.Judge Miloud has served three years on the bench after serving as a District Court Magistrate.  Her docket consists of Criminal and Civil cases as well as Domestic Relations and some Probate cases.  The Commission conducted a personal interview with Judge Miloud, reviewed opinions she authored, observed her in court, reviewed comments received from interested parties during the evaluation period, and reviewed survey responses from attorneys and non-attorneys who had experience with Judge Miloud.Meegan Miloud is a Texas native. Judge Miloud enjoys reading, cooking, and playing tennis. She received her bachelor’s degree from the University of Oklahoma in 1998 and her juris doctorate from Texas Wesleyan University School of Law in 2001. Judge Miloud is a former District Court Magistrate in the 1st Judicial District where she presided over probate matters, domestic relations, and juvenile cases.   She was formerly an Assistant District Attorney in Tarrant County, Texas and an Assistant District Attorney in Laramie County, Wyoming. Before taking the bench Judge Miloud was respondent parent counsel and Guardian ad Litem in cases of child welfare and adult mental health in the Denver metro area. Judge Miloud was Respondent Parent Counsel and a Guardian ad litem (GAL) for parents and guardians in Dependency and Neglect cases, counsel for Respondents in Mental Health, defense counsel and GAL for adult Respondents for Conservatorships and Guardianships and minors in Mental Health and Probate cases in the Denver metro area.

Poland, Andrew C. 2026 Evaluation 
 First Judicial District - District Court JudgeHonorable Andrew C. PolandRetention Year: 2026Recommendation: Meets Performance Standards
 Reports: 2026 Retention Survey Report (PDF)2025 Interim Survey Report (PDF)
 The First Judicial District Commission on Judicial Performance (the Commission) unanimously agrees by a vote of 9-0 (One Commissioner recused because the Commissioner is a party to a case pending before Judge Poland) that Judge Andrew C. Poland MEETS PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.Judge Poland is a District Court Judge in Jefferson County, appointed on June 2, 2024, and presides over a mixed docket consisting of criminal (30%), civil (40%) and domestic relations matters (30%). Feedback for Judge Poland’s performance was provided by parties, attorneys, and jurors appearing before him in court and by peers, based on his integrity, legal knowledge, communication skills, judicial temperament, administrative performance, and service to the community. Feedback recognized Judge Poland’s steady growth during his first two years on the district court bench. He was recognized for managing his courtroom, having a fair and even temperament, being deliberate, clearly explaining his rulings, and being effective in case management. Judge Poland was also described as demonstrating meaningful growth in the role, with continued opportunity to further develop and refine his legal analysis as he gains experience across a broad district court docket. Judge Poland takes all feedback and suggestions for performance improvement seriously and collaborates with his mentors and staff to address issues. Judge Poland is active in many judicial and community service initiatives including serving on the Board of Governors for the 1st Judicial District Bar Association, coordinating projects through Jefferson County Open Space and volunteering for Jefferson County High School Mock Trials.In conducting its evaluation of Judge Poland’s performance, the Commission conducted a personal interview, observed him in court, and reviewed the 2025–2026 survey responses from attorneys and non-attorneys appearing before him. The Commission additionally received feedback from the chief judge, the district attorney, and the head of the Public Defender’s Office. The Commission also reviewed Judge Poland’s self-evaluation, and three orders involving matters for which he has ruled. After completing the above reviews, the Commission finds Judge Poland meets performance criteria.Judge Poland is a native of Jefferson County, CO. He earned his Bachelor of Science degree in 2009 from Colorado State University and Juris Doctorate in 2011 from Thomas Jefferson School of Law. Prior to being appointed District Court Judge, Judge Poland practiced law privately from 2012 to 2023, focusing on juvenile defense and child welfare litigation. He served as an Instructor at Metropolitan State University from 2021 to 2023 teaching Legal Issues in Social Work Practice before serving as Magistrate in the 1st Judicial District from 2023 to 2024. His professional background reflects longstanding service to children, families, and the Jefferson County community.

Rhamey, Christopher 2026 Evaluation 
 First Judicial District - District Court JudgeHonorable Christopher RhameyRetention Year: 2026Recommendation: Meets Performance Standards
 Reports: 2026 Retention Survey Report (PDF)2025 Interim Survey Report (PDF)
 The First Judicial District Commission on Judicial Performance unanimously (9-0, 1 abstention) finds that Judge Christopher Rhamey MEETS PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.Judge Rhamey was appointed to the District Court in Jefferson County on July 31, 2023. He presides over criminal, civil, and domestic relations cases. Judge Rhamey’s demeanor is described as calm, professional, and attentive. His approach to case management is effective, and he does not have any cases open that are over eighteen months old. Judge Rhamey issues orders on motions in a timely and efficient manner, often working into the night so that he can ensure the facts of the case are fresh in his mind while he is writing his orders. He is considered to be very knowledgeable about criminal law, and other judges seek his mentorship in this area. He prepares diligently for sentencing hearings and believes it is important to balance the risk to the community against the needs of the defendant while also considering the message it sends to the community. Judge Rhamey is still growing in his knowledge of civil and domestic relations law and is actively seeking mentorship and education in these areas. It is very important to Judge Rhamey that he always asks himself – and others – how he can improve in every aspect of his job, and the Commission believes that Judge Rhamey has been and will continue to be an asset to the judicial bench.The Commission conducted a personal interview with Judge Rhamey, reviewed opinions he authored, observed him in court, reviewed comments received from interested parties during the evaluation, and reviewed survey responses from attorneys and non-attorneys who had experience with Judge Rhamey. Survey responses noted Judge Rhamey’s knowledge of the law, preparation for hearings, and willingness to learn in areas with which the judge was less familiar. There were references that his tone in written orders could be harsh. The commission took extra care to examine the judge’s orders and concluded that Judge Rhamey’s tone was appropriate.Prior to Judge Rhamey’s appointment to the bench, Judge Rhamey worked for the Adams County District Attorney’s Office where he specialized in child victim crimes and supervised nearly every unit in the office. He attended and played baseball for Pointe Loma Nazarene University in San Diego, California, then graduated from the University of Denver Sturm College of Law in 2012. Judge Rhamey worked as a youth baseball coach before becoming an attorney and continues to coach baseball for his son’s Little League team. Judge Rhamey heads all wiretaps for Jefferson County and participates in Criminal Bench Bar meetings.

 Russell, Tamara S. 2026 Evaluation 
Russell, Tamara S. 2026 Evaluation 
 First Judicial District - District Court JudgeHonorable Tamara S. RussellRetention Year: 2026Recommendation: Meets Performance Standards
 Reports: 2026 Retention Survey Report (PDF)2023 Interim Survey Report (PDF)
 The First Judicial District Commission on Judicial Performance unanimously agrees by a vote of 10-0 that Judge Tamara S. Russell MEETS PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.During most of this term, Judge Russell presided over a mixed docket including criminal, civil, and domestic relations cases. However, in February of 2026, Judge Russell’s docket switched to an all-criminal docket. Judge Russell is a highly experienced Judge and is noted to be balanced and respectful to both attorneys and litigants in her courtroom. She strives to treat each person in her courtroom equally with dignity, respect, and fairness. She demonstrates a good command of the law and the rules of evidence, and her orders are typically well-reasoned and detailed. She stays current with changes in the law, something she prioritizes and makes significant effort to do. Judge Russell aims to balance her efforts to manage court time effectively and efficiently with her judicial philosophy of allowing all parties to fully state their positions in her courtroom and be heard. Even if a litigant disagrees with her rulings, she works to have the parties feel that they are understood and that they, in turn, understand her rulings. This aim has, at times, potentially come at the expense of docket management, a component of her performance that she continues to hone.The Commission conducted a personal interview with Judge Russell, reviewed orders she authored, observed her in court, reviewed the 2020-2025 judicial performance survey responses from attorneys and non-attorneys appearing before her, received feedback from the Chief Judge of the District, as well as the District Attorney and Public Defender Office Head.  The 2026 survey results had a very limited number of responses, but a significant majority of attorneys and non-attorneys opined that Judge Russell meets performance standards. 11 appellate judges responded to the performance survey and rated Judge Russell highly (3.5 out of 4.0).Judge Russell was raised in rural Indiana and graduated from Indiana University with honors. She attended CU Law School and graduated in 1987. Most of her career has been spent in the courtroom; she worked for an insurance defense firm after law school and then became a deputy district attorney in Adams County. Subsequently, she became Chief Deputy City Attorney in Lakewood, Colorado, which lasted until she was appointed to the Jefferson County District Court bench on October 1, 2005.

Zenisek, Christopher C. 2026 Evaluation
Zenisek, Christopher C. 2026 Evaluation
 First Judicial District - District Court JudgeHonorable Christopher C. ZenisekRetention Year: 2026Recommendation: Meets Performance Standards
 Reports: 2026 Retention Survey Report (PDF)2023 Interim Survey Report (PDF)
 The First Judicial District Commission on Judicial Performance unanimously agrees by a vote of 10-0 that Judge Christopher C. Zenisek MEETS PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.Judge Zenisek is a District Court Judge in Jefferson County presiding over a mixed docket of criminal, civil, and domestic relations matters. He is consistently described as thoughtful, prepared, thorough, and fair.  He has a calm, professional demeanor that promotes respect, efficiency, and control in the courtroom.  His rulings are timely, clear, and carefully considered, reflecting strong judgment, impartiality, and accountability, and he manages complex cases with diligence and skill. He is actively engaged in the legal community through service with multiple bar organizations and Colorado Supreme Court committees, participates in mock trials with high school students, and was appointed by the Chief Justice to preside over the Marshall Fire cases while maintaining a full caseload. He was able to manage this additional responsibility without taking a reduced caseload.The Commission conducted a personal interview with Judge Zenisek, reviewed opinions he authored, observed Judge Zenisek in court, reviewed the 2025 Judicial Performance Survey Report from attorneys and non-attorneys appearing before him and received feedback from the Office of the State Public Defender and the First Judicial District Attorney's Office.
